name: academic-calendars
what_it_holds: README-only 'single source of truth' listing how to algorithmically retrieve academic-calendar dates (first/last day of instruction, finals weeks) for US universities, organized by region (West, Midwest, Northeast, South). Only 2 universities actually documented (University of Washington, Stanford) with URLs/parsing notes -- no committed CSV of term dates. 3 commits total, 0 stars, unlicensed, last touched 2020-06-08.
why_useful: If built out, a university-term-date calendar (fall move-in, spring break, finals, commencement) is a candidate seasonal regressor for ABNB nights in college markets, but this repo is too thin (2 universities, no data file) to use as-is -- flag as a stub/idea, not a working dataset.
themes: Student, seasonal-worker, medical and other niche travel-demand datasets; university calendars; military moves

name: Ecommerce-Price-Tracker
what_it_holds: Small modular Python pipeline (no stars, updated Jul 2026) that scrapes real-time prices across e-commerce sites, cleans them into structured CSV-like outputs, computes historical trend charts. No data files committed as of the check; purely a scraping/ETL template.
why_useful: Low-value on its own (no data, generic personal project) but is a concrete, current (2026) template for a lightweight scheduled price-scrape-to-timeseries pipeline, structurally similar to what would be needed for any non-Airbnb STR-price-panel scraper the team might build later.
themes: Retail and ecommerce alt-data open samples (web-scraped prices, Amazon rank), as templates for platform KPI nowcasting

name: TourismForecastReconciliation
what_it_holds: R project producing short-term tourism forecasts (ARIMA, ETS, dynamic harmonic regression, forecast reconciliation) for the Maldives, pulling directly from the Maldives Monetary Authority's public query database API (https://database.mma.gov.mv/api). Needs a user-supplied API key stored in a local Secrets.R file; no bulk data committed.
why_useful: A working, scriptable client for a national-authority tourism/monetary database (APAC/Indian Ocean tourism-dependent economy) — relevant to gap 7 (regional travel volume outside US/EU) as a template for pulling government tourism series, and gap 17 for reconciliation methodology, though the underlying data itself is Maldives-specific and probably too small a market to move ABNB directly.
time_coverage: Whatever MMA's API exposes (not stated precisely)
themes: Time-series datasets curated for tourism forecasting research (Monash, M-competitions tourism, Kaggle tourism forecasting), tourism demand models with data

name: nycdb/nycdb
what_it_holds: Python program that downloads, processes, and loads 40+ NYC public housing/property datasets into a single PostgreSQL database in one command: PLUTO (parcel-level land use, ~857k lots), DOB job filings/complaints/violations/vacate orders/certificates of occupancy, HPD violations/registrations/litigations/complaints, DOF Rolling Sales and Tax Lien Sales, ACRIS (deeds and mortgage documents), Evictions, ECB Violations, Property Address Directory, rodent inspections, subsidized-housing database, corporate/ownership records. 796 commits, code AGPLv3, prebuilt database files CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
why_useful: Not Airbnb data itself, but a ready-made, one-command acquisition method for NYC housing/regulatory context (gap #13 housing/host-supply economics; possibly a path to NYC OSE short-term-rental registration counts if/when that dataset is added to its source list) -- useful as tooling to pull city registries around the LL18 period rather than as a direct Inside-Airbnb substitute.
time_coverage: current + historical NYC open-data extracts, varies by dataset
size_hint: n/a (pulls from NYC Open Data at run time)
last_activity: actively maintained as of recent GitHub search
duplicate_of_holding: We already hold the NYC OSE STR registry directly per CONTEXT.md; nycdb is a broader general-purpose NYC housing-data puller, not a duplicate of that specific dataset.
themes: Inside Airbnb New York City snapshots around Local Law 18 (2023-06 to 2024-03) stored in repos
Housing supply and investor activity: building permits, Redfin investor purchases, mortgage rates, county assessor/parcel data, LLC ownership, NYC PLUTO/ACRIS
Housing affordability and STR-housing studies data: rent-burden, vacancy, STR share of housing stock by tract
why_all: Not Airbnb data itself, but a ready-made, one-command acquisition method for NYC housing/regulatory context (gap #13 housing/host-supply economics; possibly a path to NYC OSE short-term-rental registration counts if/when that dataset is added to its source list) -- useful as tooling to pull city registries around the LL18 period rather than as a direct Inside-Airbnb substitute.

Directly fills gap 13 (long-term rental/housing supply economics) and touches NYC PLUTO/ACRIS specifically named in the theme; a one-command ingest of parcel, permit, ownership, sales and rent-registration data for the largest ABNB metro, letting the team build NYC host-supply/LTR-STR crossover series without hand-scraping NYC Open Data endpoints one by one.

Rent Stabilization Unit Counts by building/year is the closest free proxy to 'STR share of housing stock' logic in reverse (regulated long-term supply vs. STR conversion pressure) for NYC, one of our 13 Inside Airbnb panel cities; evictions + HPD violations give a rent-burden/housing-distress proxy at building/tract level to pair with STR registry data (gap #13, also touches #8/#12 municipal registries we already hold for NYC OSE).
